page: Amazon Web Services r7i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyper-threading with two threads per core. Memory capacity is 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Passmark CPU testing, Passmark CPU encryption, Geekbench ray tracing, and image processing. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the top 25% tier, while single-core performance is average. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, consistently rank in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the processor supports Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which contribute to strong prompt processing speeds in LLM inference benchmarks across small, medium, and large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r7i.24xlarge offers high resource density for memory-intensive applications, though the lack of local NVMe storage requires external storage provisioning, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The high-speed DDR5 memory and strong multi-threaded capabilities make this instance highly suitable for large-scale database operations, in-memory caches like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
